deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is a heavily corrected draft of a formal letter by Riemann to a high official, addressed as 'Hochwohlgeborner, Hochzuverehrender Herr Geheimer Rath'. The addressee is presumably someone connected with the Hannoverian university administration (the 'hohes Curatorium'). The letter is signed 'B. Riemann, Professor der Mathematik', dated only 'Göttingen den', and has a false start that was struck through.

Content, in paraphrase:
(1) During a recent visit (originally 'in Hannover', later struck) Riemann heard that the university might entrust him with representing theoretical astronomy at Göttingen. Such a post would match his earlier wishes.
(2) For some years the observatory has been in the hands of Dr. Westphal and Dr. Klinkerfues. In that time Riemann has almost entirely set astronomy aside, dealing with astronomical topics only insofar as they belong to higher mathematics.
(3) The Curatorium has already kindly assigned him an apartment at the observatory. Even so, under present conditions it is very hard for him to learn the details of practical astronomy, which a representative of astronomy must know.
(4) He would like to work his way into practical astronomy under an older astronomer, whose name is illegible and perhaps elsewhere. To this end he asks the Curatorium to grant him a scientific journey or a 'Volontair' position.
(5) He hesitated to make this request because he was only recently promoted to ordentlicher Professor ('Ernennung' struck, 'Beförderung' inserted). However, the later he starts, the harder it will become to master practical astronomy.
(6) He fears his request may encroach on Dr. Klinkerfues, and he acknowledges the difficulties involved.
(7) He cannot judge whether other considerations stand in the way. He has therefore first consulted two senior colleagues: a 'Hofrath W...' and 'Professor Weber'.
(8) If the addressee comes to Göttingen soon, as Riemann has heard rumoured, Riemann will call on him to receive his answer in person.

Dating, by inference (mine): the promotion to Ordinarius in July 1859, after Dirichlet's death, and the apartment in the Sternwarte (mentioned by Dedekind) point to roughly 1859–1860.

The neighbouring pages are an unrelated reuse of paper. The previous page has the shock-wave/Riemann-invariant notes (f(ρ)±u = 2r, 2s) plus private business letters. The next page has the value of k = c/c' for air and a fragment on angular-momentum integrals in the three-body problem. Neither relates to this letter.

deep.surprise_reason: No mathematics. The letter is a minor biographical item. Riemann's residence at the Sternwarte and the post-Gauss arrangement with Klinkerfues and Westphal are known. His explicit wish to take over theoretical astronomy and to train in practical astronomy is a small, possibly unpublished biographical detail, not a mathematical result.
transcription_corrections: The first consulted person is very likely not a second 'Weber'. The image reads something like 'Herrn Hofrath W[ö/i]..h' (possibly Wöhler) 'und Herrn Professor Weber'. The machine transcription's 'Hofrath Weber[?] und Professor Weber[?]' should not be trusted.

The insertion near 'in das Gebiet der höheren Mathematik fällt' is closer to 'ein Gebiet für den Mathematiker' / 'das Gebiet der Mathematik'. It is an alternative phrasing written above the line, not additional text.
'durch die Ernennung' is struck and replaced by 'Beförderung' ('durch die Beförderung zum ordentlichen Professor'). This matches the image.
The long struck passage near the end (about the two consulted men being trustworthy and well informed) is largely illegible. The machine's reconstruction there is conjectural.
The isolated fragment ', ob eine Volontairstelle zu einer wissenschaftlichen Reise' is a marginal or alternative formulation of the request. It is not a separate sentence of the final text.
